passage.title: The spread of paper
passage.text: Paper was first made in China about two thousand years ago. Early papermakers soaked plant fibres, such as bark and old rags, in water until they became a soft pulp. They spread the pulp across a flat screen and let the water drain away. The thin layer left behind was pressed and dried in the sun to form a sheet. The method spread slowly along trade routes, reaching Europe more than a thousand years later. Before then, most European books were written on animal skin, which was costly and slow to prepare. Cheaper paper made it practical to print books in large numbers.
